question.question:
A firm must choose between two mutually exclusive projects evaluated at an annual discount rate of 5 percent; every cash flow other than the time-zero outlay occurs at a year-end. Project A costs USD 7000 at time zero, generates USD 3600 of revenue at the end of each of its 3 years, and in addition to that final year's revenue has a signed terminal cash flow of USD -800 at the end of year 3, where a positive figure is a salvage receipt and a negative figure is a decommissioning payment. Project B costs USD 6500 at time zero and lasts 5 years with no terminal cash flow; its engineers report the change in annual operating cost as USD 500 per year, where a negative figure is a cost reduction that counts as a year-end cash inflow of the same magnitude and a positive figure is a cost increase that counts as a year-end outflow of the same magnitude. Compute each project's NPV, convert each NPV to an equivalent annual annuity (EAA) over that project's own life at the stated rate, and identify the larger of the two EAAs. Decision rule: if both NPVs are zero or negative, choose neither project; otherwise choose the project with the larger EAA, with ties going to Project A. Which project should be chosen?

Answer format: return exactly one of these case-sensitive tokens and no additional text: `project_a`, `project_b`, `neither`.

slots.description: NPV of Project A including the signed terminal cash flow
NPV of Project B using the stated operating-cost sign convention
The larger of the two equivalent annual annuities
